title: API Canvas
pitch: API Canvas is a local-first WebMCP workspace where people and agents can discover public data, connect APIs,create reusable cards and visualizations,and reason across the resulting dashboard together.
about_excerpt: API Canvas is a local-first WebMCP workspace where people and agents can discover public data, connect APIs,create reusable cards and visualizations,and reason across the resulting dashboard together. Like Comment Story Updates Api Canvas build a dashboard Canvas View Inspiration Building a useful dashboard usually involves a surprising amount of repetitive work. You have to find an API, understand its documentation, construct the request, inspect the response, identify useful fields, create a visualization, connect those fields to a component, and repeat the process for every additional source. I wanted to see whether WebMCP could make that process dramatically more direct. Instead of only asking: "Can an agent operate this application?" API Canvas asks: "Can an agent help construct the application experience using primitives the website intentionally exposes?" What I Built API Canvas is a local-first workspace for turning public data into reusable connected cards. A dashboard can contain components such as: Tables Charts Maps Metrics Lists Notes Text and explanation blocks Search results Media Raw datasets API responses Question blocks Agent-generated answer blocks Sources and presentation are kept separate. That means one API response can power several different visualizations without repeatedly requesting the data. Users can also transform and combine information through declarative mappings including filtering, sorting, grouping, arithmetic, field selection, and joins. WebMCP Tools API Canvas exposes a large WebMCP tool surface covering dashboard and data workflows. An agent can perform operations such as: Create or switch dashboards Add data sources Request public API data Add cards Select appropriate visualizations Connect source fields to cards Transform data Update layout Resize or reorder cards Inspect dashboard state Read selected cards Answer questions using dashboard context Create new explanation blocks Export or present results This lets a simple request expand into a multi-step application workflow. For example: Build me an earthquake research dashboard. Find magnitude 5 or greater earthquakes from the past week, map the events, create a table, identify the strongest earthquake, and summarize it. API Canvas can break that request into structured operations and leave behind a real editable dashboard. Why WebMCP Dashboard construction is naturally compositional. The user usually knows the outcome they want but should not need to manually specify every intermediate API call and UI operation. WebMCP lets the application expose those intermediate operations directly. The agent gets structured tools instead of having to simulate: click Add Card → select source → open another menu → map a field → choose visualization → repeat. This makes workflows faster and substantially easier for an agent to reason about. Human + Agent Collaboration The most interesting part of API Canvas is that the resulting dashboard becomes shared context. Imagine the agent has created an earthquake dashboard containing a map, table, and several metrics. The user can then ask: Using all of the information currently on this page, which earthquake was strongest? The agent can inspect the existing structured cards, reason across them, produce an answer, and create another normal dashboard card containing that explanation. The workflow becomes: Data → Visualization → Context → Reasoning → New Visualization Everything remains editable by the human. How I Built It API Canvas is built with Vue 3, Vite, Pinia, IndexedDB, ECharts, AJV, and WebMCP. The workspace has a reusable block system that separates: data sources raw responses normalized values transformations bindings presentation The normal UI and WebMCP tools call into the same underlying workspace actions. AJV validates structured WebMCP inputs. IndexedDB stores larger browser-local response caches and workspace information. Public data adapters support structured formats including JSON, CSV, XML, feeds, permitted HTML tables, and embedded JSON. The application intentionally does not provide an unrestricted proxy or execute arbitrary supplied scripts. The /webmcp documentation page is generated from the same canonical WebMCP contracts used by the application. Challenges I Faced The largest challenge was building something generic without making it unpredictable. An unrestricted "call any API and run any code" tool would be powerful but would also make the application difficult to reason about. Instead, API Canvas uses bounded requests, validated schemas, explicit source handling, and declarative transformations. Another challenge was keeping data, provenance, presentation, and transformations sufficiently independent. That separation is what allows an agent to replace a chart with a table without losing the underlying source. What I Learned API Canvas changed how I think about agent interfaces. The visual dashboard does not need to be replaced by chat. Instead, the dashboard can become the persistent shared artifact that the human and agent construct together. WebMCP then acts as the structured editing and orchestration layer. What's Next I would like to expand API Canvas with more public data adapters, richer visualization components, reusable dashboard templates, local analytical queries, and collaborative sharing. The broader idea is an open, composable workspace where agents can assemble useful specialized interfaces on demand.
